local:agnix-tags-are-annotated-and-unsor.title:
TWO probe traps live on this repo's tag list, both hit on the 0.49.0
bump and both recorded in `sources/agnix.manifest`.

1. **The tags are ANNOTATED.** `git ls-remote --tags --refs .../agnix v0.49.0`
   returns `dc388699…`, which is the TAG OBJECT, not the commit. The commit is
   `b0401135…` (`gh api repos/agent-sh/agnix/commits/v0.49.0 --jq .sha`). Two
   routes, two different 40-hex strings, and only one of them is a commit — a
   manifest pinned to the tag object still clones, so nothing would have
   reported it. Contrast graphify and datamodel-code-generator, whose
   lightweight tags make both routes agree.

2. **The tag list is not sorted by version.** `git ls-remote --tags` ends at
   `v0.9.3`, which reads like the latest and is THREE MINORS behind v0.49.0.
   Ask `gh api repos/agent-sh/agnix/releases/latest --jq .tag_name` instead.
   This is a display-order bound wearing the clothes of an answer — exactly
   `probes-need-a-control-arm.md` rule 3.

Re-probe both on each bump: an upstream that switches to lightweight tags
retires (1), and nothing retires (2) short of a version-sorted listing.
